issues.description: preview_fn has no stated contract: purity, side effects, failure semantics, or input/output access are all unspecified
issues.detail: The docs introduce preview_fn without preconditions, postconditions, or failure mode, then admit it cannot see node inputs/outputs and punt with 'wrap in try-except if needed.' Readers cannot reason about what preview() returns on failure, whether it must be pure, or what value is actually being previewed. Specify the contract; do not paper over it with defensive-programming advice.

issues.description: meta field complects renderer configuration with descriptive metadata under one name
issues.detail: The same meta dict carries Mermaid layout/textStyle renderer directives and arbitrary user metadata like timestamps and versions. The docs later concede meta serves 'two purposes,' leaving readers to guess which keys are reserved versus passthrough. Split renderer hints from value metadata, or at minimum annotate which keys are Mermaid passthrough versus Kedro-Viz extensions.

issues.description: Basic-usage example uses obscure `next(n for n in pipeline.nodes)` over a generator
issues.detail: The retrieval is equivalent to `pipeline.nodes[0]` written obscurely, with no stated invariant about node ordering. A tutorial should teach plain indexing or explicit name lookup, not a needlessly clever generator expression whose postcondition is unstated. Replace with `pipeline.nodes[0]` or a name-based lookup.

issues.description: Closure example for 'data context' hides the late-binding hazard and freezes a sample at construction time
issues.detail: The make_preview_fn pattern captures sample_data by reference at pipeline-construction time, then is invoked later as if live. Docs neither warn that mutation of the captured object silently changes preview output nor state when the snapshot was taken. Name the binding hazard and clarify the snapshot's identity in time.

issues.description: ImagePreview example places a commented alternative after the `return` statement
issues.detail: Illustrating an alternative as dead code after `return` teaches sloppy control flow even in documentation. Split the two encodings into two distinct example functions, or parameterize a single example with an if/else, so readers do not pause over apparent unreachable code.

issues.description: Experimental warning is present but docs specify meta schemas, renderer_key, and subclass set as if stable
issues.detail: The top-of-page experimental notice is correct, but the rest of the page documents meta keys, renderer_key semantics, and seven preview subclasses with stable-looking precision. Readers will build against these. Flag explicitly which surfaces are likely to move — subclass set, meta schema, renderer_key contract — and consider whether one tagged Preview value would replace the seven subclasses.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on a documentation patch that teaches the surface of preview_fn competently but ships several unreasoned design choices as 'best practice.' The central failing is that preview_fn is introduced without a stated contract — purity, failure semantics, and access to node inputs/outputs are all unspecified, and the docs paper over the gap with defensive try-except advice. The meta field complects renderer configuration with descriptive metadata, and key examples teach footguns: obscure `next()` retrieval, unreachable code after `return`, and closure capture without the late-binding warning. Fixes are mostly mechanical prose edits, but the contract and meta-split questions warrant a design note before stabilizing the API.
